$comment: Tests that are tracked, real, and NOT YET REPAIRED.
This list is the replacement for the 21 silent testPathIgnorePatterns entries
that used to live in jest.config.js. The difference is not cosmetic:
- it is the SINGLE source of truth (jest.config.js reads this file),
- every entry states the root cause and the repair, in the open,
- `npm run test:quarantine` runs exactly these files, so their real state
is one command away instead of invisible,
- CI runs that command and prints the result on every build,
- scripts/check-test-discovery.js reports them as NOT COVERAGE and fails
the build if this list grows past `ceiling`.
A file here does not count as coverage. Adding one is a visible, reviewable
diff that must also raise `ceiling` — which is the point. The number only
This is not a place to park a failing test. It is a debt register with a
balance, and the balance is meant to reach zero.

files.cause: stale API contract — superseded delivery mechanism
files.detail: All 29 cases drive POST /api/ai-chatbot/process. ai-chatbot.routes.js exists but is required by nothing, so the route is not mounted and every request 404s. message-worker.js replaced that HTTP entry point with a direct call and says so at line 7.
files.repair: Retarget the suite at AIChatbotController.processNewIntent(message, history, entities, language, aiSettings, ingestionResult, imageUrls) — the function message-worker actually calls — and assert on its returned { response, confidence, source, grounding } instead of res.body. The mocks (rag.service, llm.service, entities) already fit; the input shape and assertions are the work.
files.meanwhile: The happy path through this pipeline is covered end-to-end by tests/meta-e2e (real signed webhook → real queue → worker → grounding gate). The confidence gate, FAQ threshold and input-validation branches are NOT covered anywhere.

files.cause: wrong test framework + bad import paths + destructive setup
files.detail: Written for Mocha/chai: uses `before()` and 35 `.to.be`-style assertions, and chai is not a dependency of this project. Its three imports are all wrong from tests/ — '../../src/app' resolves above the backend root, and '../../src/config/database' names a file that does not exist. It also calls sequelize.sync({ force: true }), which drops every table.
files.repair: Convert `before` → `beforeAll` and chai assertions → jest expect; fix the three require paths; then rename to *.integration.test.js so it runs under jest.integration.config.js, whose env.js refuses to start against a database that is not provably disposable. It must NOT be enabled in the unit gate: the force-sync would run against whatever DATABASE_URL happens to be set.
files.meanwhile: Payment detection is covered by payment-processing-reconciliation.security.test.js and self-mfs-handler.media-security.test.js in the security gate; the three merchant scenarios in this file are not covered.
